review_notes: I read the whole file and concentrated on its simp, fun_prop and continuity attributes. I checked the nearby Homeomorph/Defs `coe_toEquiv` lemma and searched Mathlib for existing coercion lemmas and uses of the associativity and four-way-commutativity homeomorphisms. Most simp annotations here look fine, for example `continuous_prodMk` and `map_fst_nhds`. The gaps I found are in the Homeomorph section: the simp lemmas for several homeomorphisms are stated through `toEquiv`, which is not the normal form simp reaches for coerced function applications. I did not run Lean, so I did not test whether these gaps cause simp failures in practice. Whether a missing lemma matters also depends on how the unfolding behaves in practice, and `rfl`-based goals may still close without it.

findings.excerpt: lemma prodAssoc_toEquiv : (prodAssoc X Y Z).toEquiv = Equiv.prodAssoc X Y Z := rfl
findings.problem: For `prodAssoc`, `sumAssoc`, `prodProdProdComm` and `sumSumSumComm`, the simp lemmas are only stated for the bare `.toEquiv` (`prodAssoc_toEquiv`, `sumAssoc_toEquiv`, `sumSumSumComm_toEquiv`). `prodProdProdComm` has no coercion or `toEquiv` lemma at all, only `_symm`. The simp normal form of a homeomorphism applied to a point is `⇑h` (`Homeomorph.coe_toEquiv` rewrites `⇑h.toEquiv` to `⇑h`). A goal such as `Homeomorph.prodAssoc X Y Z ((a, b), c) = (a, b, c)`, or `⇑(Homeomorph.prodAssoc ..) = ...`, therefore has no simp lemma to unfold it. The siblings `prodComm`/`sumComm` (`coe_prodComm`, `coe_sumComm`) and `punitProd` (`coe_punitProd`) do have coercion lemmas, so the interface is inconsistent. Outside this file the `prodAssoc` and `prodProdProdComm` homeomorphisms are only used through `comp_continuous_iff'` and `isEmbedding`, which may be why the gap went unnoticed.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` coercion lemmas in the same style as `coe_prodComm`, for example `theorem coe_prodAssoc : ⇑(prodAssoc X Y Z) = Equiv.prodAssoc X Y Z := rfl`, and likewise `coe_prodProdProdComm`, `coe_sumAssoc` and `coe_sumSumSumComm`. Alternatively mark the definitions `@[simps! -fullyApplied apply]`, as `prodPUnit` does. Add symm companions where they are missing, for example for `prodAssoc` and `sumAssoc`.
findings.benefit: Simp can unfold applications of these homeomorphisms to the underlying `Equiv` and then to explicit tuples or `Sum` terms. This makes the interface uniform across the `Homeomorph` section.

findings.excerpt: @[simp] theorem coe_emptySum [IsEmpty Y] : (emptySum X Y).toEquiv = Equiv.emptySum Y X := rfl
findings.problem: The name `coe_emptySum` suggests a statement about the function coercion, but the statement is about `.toEquiv`, so it is really an `emptySum_toEquiv` lemma. No lemma describes `⇑(emptySum X Y)`, and `emptySum` has no `simps`-generated lemmas, unlike `sumEmpty` (`@[simps! -fullyApplied apply]`). Simp therefore cannot compute `Homeomorph.emptySum X Y (Sum.inr x)`. The neighbouring `coe_sumComm`, `coe_punitProd` and `coe_prodComm` do state the coercion form.
findings.proposed_change: Rename the existing lemma to `emptySum_toEquiv`, or keep it only as a toEquiv simp lemma. Add `@[simp] theorem coe_emptySum [IsEmpty Y] : ⇑(emptySum X Y) = Equiv.emptySum Y X := rfl`, or put `@[simps! -fullyApplied apply]` on `emptySum`. The new `coe_emptySum` should match the naming used by `coe_sumComm`.
findings.benefit: The simp set can reduce `emptySum` applications to `Sum.elim`/`Sum.inr` terms, as it can for `sumEmpty`, and the name matches what the lemma states.

findings.excerpt:
def sumCongr (h₁ : X ≃ₜ X') (h₂ : Y ≃ₜ Y') : X ⊕ Y ≃ₜ X' ⊕ Y' where
  toEquiv := h₁.toEquiv.sumCongr h₂.toEquiv
findings.problem: The simp interfaces of `prodCongr` and `sumCongr` are asymmetric. `sumCongr` has `sumCongr_symm`, `sumCongr_refl` and `sumCongr_trans`, but no coercion lemma such as `⇑(sumCongr h₁ h₂) = Sum.map h₁ h₂`. `prodCongr` has `prodCongr_symm` and `coe_prodCongr` (to `Prod.map`), but no `prodCongr_refl` or `prodCongr_trans`. A simp call on `(prodCongr (.refl X) (.refl Y))` or on `(prodCongr h₁ h₂).trans (prodCongr h₃ h₄)` therefore does not normalize, while the corresponding `sumCongr` terms do. I found no such lemma elsewhere in Mathlib's Topology directory. The file's own comment says it presents the product and sum cases in parallel.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem coe_sumCongr : ⇑(sumCongr h₁ h₂) = Sum.map h₁ h₂ := rfl`, and add `@[simp] prodCongr_refl : prodCongr (.refl X) (.refl Y) = .refl (X × Y)` and `@[simp] prodCongr_trans` with the same shape as `sumCongr_trans`. The proofs would probably be the same `ext`/`rfl` pattern used for `sumCongr_refl`; I have not checked this.
findings.benefit: Composites and identities of product and sum homeomorphisms simplify the same way in both constructions. Applications of `sumCongr` also reduce to `Sum.map`, matching `Prod.map` for `prodCongr`.
